After the change, the 268 s of variable time splits as follows:

- ~77 s: pinned app timings, the one test per constant: the stalled load (F4),
  the node-start backoff 1+2+4+8+16 s (F8), and Try-now waiting out the real
  backoff to attempt 4.
- ~51 s: the F6 page's own schedule (synthetic click at +4 s, then a 1 s
  settle) and its absence windows.
- ~73 s: gestures, rotation, the keyboard and layout settling (F9/F12/F13/
  F15). A slow swipe plus XCUITest's idle wait is 2.6–3 s, and Status alone
  swipes five times.
- ~19 s: F8's node-start absence windows.
- ~27 s: everything else.

*Landed* (`l1: share one settled F6 run…`): four F6 tests launched
identically, waited for the same settle and then only read the instruments.
They now share one snapshot of that run: report, counters and journal. Each
still asserts its own claim under its own name. The run is cached only if it
settled, and a test run alone takes its own launch (checked:
`testThePageCannotWidenTheAllowlist` alone passes in 16.4 s). One
`test-offline.sh --build`: **609 s → 569 s**, 38 names identical (diffed),
all passing.

*Rejected after inspection:*

- **Firing the F6 page's synthetic click as soon as its markers exist.** The
  fixed +4 s is also the negatives' observation window ("every off-origin
  load it makes has been asked for by then"). The positive control, with no
  rule list and so no markers, would have kept the full window.
- **Faster inset/shell report cadence.** "Several reports in" is the layout
  settle itself.
- **Shortening the absence sleeps** (logging refusal +10 s/+5 s, redirect 3 s,
  blocked image 3 s, rule compile 2+2 s). Each is the evidence that nothing
  happened.
- **Folding the sign-in pass into the suite pass** (~5 s). R1 needs it last,
  and XCTest orders by name.
- **Skipping terminates.** The next `launch()` pays the same cost.

*What is left, and what F14 would buy.* After this, 43 launches are ~297 s of
launch and terminate, plus ~26 s outside the tests: **~320 s serial floor with
zero variable time**. Add the ~77 s of pinned timings and L1 cannot go below
~400 s serially without fewer launches, which is §3's ruled-out merging. The
240 s budget is therefore unreachable serially, and §4.2's scaling has little
left to act on in L1: the only long timers are the pinned ones. The remaining
lever is §3's parallel harness: per-simulator ports plumbed into the launch
arguments and the certificate SANs, plus per-instance fake-dashboard and proxy
control state. The ideal wall time is ~26 s + max(38 s, 544 s ÷ N):
~160 s at N = 4 and ~95 s at N = 8, on this 20-core M1 Ultra. The ideal does
not include simulator contention, which is unmeasured. The longest test
(38 s) bounds it below at ~65 s. §2's "L1 under 90 s" needs N ≥ 8, and even
then only if contention is small.

**2026-09-25, simulator contention measured: F14 reaches 240 s at N = 4.**
The projection above assumed simulators do not slow each other. This measures
that, with `scripts/bench-sim-contention.py` (run `simbench-logs/20260925-043549`,
all rounds passing). It times L1's own fixed cost: `testAFirstLaunchExplainsItself`
(an XCUITest launch into the gate, four checks, a terminate). It runs with
`-test-iterations 10` on N dedicated iPhone 17 simulators at once, one
`xcodebuild test-without-building` each. The gate needs no node and no
certificates. One stub answering 200 on the two control ports satisfies every
simulator's `setUp`. Confounders kept out: all 12 simulators were booted and
settled before anything was timed, and a warm-up round was discarded. Iteration
1 of each run (the cold launch after install) is dropped, so install is in no
number. Only iterations wholly inside the window where all N ran are counted. A
closing N = 1 round came in at 0.97× the first, so there was no drift. No
thermal warning was recorded in any round. N = 1 ran with the other 11
simulators booted and idle; a two-simulator smoke run gave the same 6.7 s.

| N | kept | test median s (p25–p75, max) | launch to usable s | × N=1 | launches/s, all sims | speedup | per-sim efficiency | CPU busy median/max % | swap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9 | 6.66 (6.53–6.92, 7.23) | 5.36 | 1.00 | 0.142 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 37/60 | 0 |
| 2 | 17 | 6.78 (6.63–6.85, 7.02) | 5.41 | 1.02 | 0.275 | 1.94 | 0.97 | 42/84 | 0 |
| 4 | 33 | 7.08 (7.02–7.19, 9.40) | 5.68 | 1.06 | 0.526 | 3.71 | 0.93 | 56/98 | 0 |
| 6 | 49 | 7.26 (7.17–7.40, 8.33) | 5.73 | 1.09 | 0.738 | 5.20 | 0.87 | 71/100 | 0 |
| 8 | 65 | 7.61 (7.52–7.77, 8.57) | 6.03 | 1.14 | 0.945 | 6.66 | 0.83 | 89/100 | 0 |
| 12 | 91 | 7.87 (7.72–8.36, 19.15) | 6.21 | 1.18 | 1.207 | 8.50 | 0.71 | 100/100 | 153 MB |

"Launch to usable" runs from XCUITest's `Open` to the first UI query. Terminate
is 1.05–1.08 s at every N. Speedup is measured throughput, which is lower than
N ÷ (× N=1) because it also counts stragglers.

- **Contention is real but modest up to 8.** A launch costs 6 % more at N = 4
  and 14 % more at N = 8. Adding simulators stops paying at **N ≈ 8**. Each one
  added from 2 to 8 returns 0.7–0.9 of a simulator. From 8 to 12 each returns
  0.46. At N = 8 the CPU is 89 % busy at the median. At N = 12 it is pinned at
  100 %, swapping starts, and a straggler takes 19 s.
- **Memory is not the limit.** Twelve booted simulators took
  `kern.memorystatus_level` from 87 to ~50 (about 1.8 GB each of 64 GB), and
  nothing swapped below N = 12.
- **Booting is the expensive part, and it must stay out of the run.** One
  first boot takes 20–23 s. Twelve at once took 70–343 s each, then 8 min
  before the host dropped under 25 % busy. F14's simulators must stay booted
  between runs, or be booted one at a time, never all at once inside L1.
- **Per-shard `xcodebuild` spin-up,** including installing the app and runner,
  grows from 6.1 s at N = 1 to 8.7 s (max) at N = 8: about +3 s of wall time.

*Corrected L1 projection* (replacing ~160 s / ~95 s). The model is 26 s outside
the tests plus the longest-first packing of the 38 per-test times ("after"
column above) onto N simulators. The low figure slows only each test's
launch/terminate share, by × N=1. The high figure slows whole tests by the
throughput loss. The high figure is pessimistic: most variable time is timers
and sleeps, which do not contend.

| N | no contention | measured contention |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 300 s | 303–309 s |
| 4 | 164 s | **168–175 s** |
| 6 | 118 s | 123–133 s |
| 8 | 97 s | **103–111 s** |
| 12 | 73 s | 79–93 s (CPU-saturated, swapping) |

Add ~3 s for the slower spin-up at N ≥ 4. **F14 can reach the 240 s budget: N
= 4 gives ~170–180 s, with room for the suite to grow.** N = 3 interpolates to
~215 s, which leaves too little margin. §2's "under 90 s" is not reachable on
this host. It would take N = 12, which saturates the CPU and swaps, and the
38 s longest test × 1.18 bounds it at ~71 s anyway. N = 8 (~105–115 s) is
where the curve stops paying.

Not covered by this measurement:

- The gate has no WebView. Most L1 launches also start WebKit's three
  processes (§9: ~6.0 s to idle, against 5.0 s), so page launches may contend
  somewhat more than measured. The high column is meant to absorb that.
- It says nothing about the per-instance harness state F14 has to build.
- The sandbox hid the host's process list, so nothing other than the idle 8 %
  baseline and CPU samples before each round could be attributed. The 1-minute
  load average (500–1000) counts simulator threads and is not comparable to the
  20 cores.

1	# Offline test harness: a stub SOCKS5 proxy in front of a fake dashboard.
2	#
3	# Runs with no Tailscale account, no tailnet and no network. The point is to
4	# exercise the WKWebView -> SOCKS5 -> HTTPS -> WebSocket/SSE path -- and the
5	# anti-leak negative case -- deterministically and in seconds.
6	#
7	#   make harness-up      start both, write pidfiles, wait until listening
8	#   make harness-down    stop both
9	#   make harness-status  what is running
10	#   make certs           mint the test CA + leaf (idempotent)
11	#   make trust           teach the booted simulator to trust the test CA
12	#   make bundle          fetch the pinned KiroCrew wheel into .cache (verified)
13	#   make gateway-up      start the fake KiroCrew gateway (real pinned bundle, M4)
14	#   make gateway-down    stop it
15	#   make gateway-check   its host-side contract self-test (starts and stops it)
16	#
17	# The fake gateway is separate from harness-up on purpose: it refuses to start
18	# unless its bundle is the pinned one, and a missing or wrong bundle must not
19	# take the offline (L1) suite down with it.
20	#
21	# BLACKHOLE=1 starts the proxy in refuse-every-CONNECT mode, which is the
22	# negative fixture: the page load must FAIL rather than quietly succeeding by
23	# some direct route.
24	
25	PY           ?= python3
26	PROXY_PORT   ?= 1080
27	PROXY_CONTROL_PORT ?= 1081
28	DASH_PORT    ?= 8443
29	DASH_CONTROL_PORT  ?= 8480
30	GW_PORT      ?= 8444
31	GW_CONTROL_PORT ?= 8481
32	GW_EXPIRE_IN ?= 0
33	PROXY_USER   ?= tsnet
34	PROXY_PASS   ?= s3cret
35	DASH_HOST    ?= dash.tail-scale.ts.net
36	RUN_DIR      ?= .run
37	JOURNAL      ?= $(RUN_DIR)/proxy.ndjson
38	BLACKHOLE    ?= 0
39	
40	PROXY_PID    := $(RUN_DIR)/socks5.pid
41	DASH_PID     := $(RUN_DIR)/dashboard.pid
42	PROXY_LOG    := $(RUN_DIR)/socks5.log
43	DASH_LOG     := $(RUN_DIR)/dashboard.log
44	GW_PID       := $(RUN_DIR)/gateway.pid
45	GW_LOG       := $(RUN_DIR)/gateway.log
46	
47	# F6 §6: the hosts /single-origin reaches for besides the away origin. Under
48	# -ProxyEverything each would be SERVED -- and counted by Host -- by the fake
49	# dashboard if the app's rule list allowed it, and none can reach the real
50	# host. dash.tail-scale.ts.net:8444 is the port probe (a gateway rule that
51	# forgot the port); it is a map key, unrelated to GW_PORT's listener.
52	F6_MAPS := $(foreach hp,dash.tail-scale.ts.net:8444 esm.sh:443 esm.sh.away.example:443 \
53	             esm.shady.example:443 esm.sh:8444 fonts.googleapis.com:443 fonts.gstatic.com:443, \
54	             --map $(hp)=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT))
55	
56	ifeq ($(BLACKHOLE),1)
57	  BLACKHOLE_FLAG := --blackhole
58	else
59	  BLACKHOLE_FLAG :=
60	endif
61	
62	.PHONY: certs
63	certs:  ## Mint the test CA and leaf (no-op if present and unexpired)
64		@./gen-certs.sh
65	
66	.PHONY: trust
67	trust: certs  ## Trust the test CA in the booted simulator
68		@xcrun simctl keychain booted add-root-cert "$(CURDIR)/ca.der"
69		@echo "::: test CA trusted in the booted simulator :::"
70	
71	.PHONY: harness-up
72	harness-up: certs harness-down  ## Start the fake dashboard + stub proxy
73		@mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)
74		@# Refuse to start on top of someone else's listener.
75		@#
76		@# This is not hypothetical: a dashboard left over from an earlier session
77		@# was still holding :$(DASH_PORT), serving a certificate minted before the
78		@# current CA. The replacement died instantly on "address already in use",
79		@# a port probe saw the STRANGER still listening and reported the harness
80		@# healthy, and every TLS check then failed with "unable to get local
81		@# issuer certificate" -- which reads like a certificate bug and is not.
82		@for port in $(DASH_PORT) $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) $(PROXY_PORT) $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT); do \
83		    pids=$$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); \
84		    if [ -n "$$pids" ]; then \
85		        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is already in use by pid(s): $$pids" >&2; \
86		        echo "       These are probably strays from an earlier run." >&2; \
87		        echo "       Stop them with: make harness-reap" >&2; \
88		        exit 1; \
89		    fi; \
90		done
91		@# Truncate the journal so an assertion can't pass on a previous run's
92		@# connect events -- the exact way this kind of test rots into a no-op.
93		@: > $(JOURNAL)
94		@$(PY) dashboard.py --port $(DASH_PORT) --control-port $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) \
95			--cert server.pem --key server.key > $(DASH_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(DASH_PID)
96		@$(PY) socks5stub.py --port $(PROXY_PORT) \
97			--user $(PROXY_USER) --password $(PROXY_PASS) \
98			--journal $(JOURNAL) $(BLACKHOLE_FLAG) --control-port $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT) \
99			--map $(DASH_HOST):443=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) \
100			--map wrong.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) \
101			--map down.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:9 \
102			--map gw.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:$(GW_PORT) \
103			$(F6_MAPS) \
104			> $(PROXY_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(PROXY_PID)
105		@# Wait for OUR processes to listen. Checking the port alone is what let
106		@# the stray above masquerade as a healthy harness, so verify the pid we
107		@# started is both alive and the one holding the port.
108		@for spec in "$(DASH_PORT):$(DASH_PID):$(DASH_LOG)" "$(PROXY_PORT):$(PROXY_PID):$(PROXY_LOG)"; do \
109		    port=$${spec%%:*}; rest=$${spec#*:}; pidfile=$${rest%%:*}; log=$${rest#*:}; \
110		    pid=$$(cat $$pidfile); \
111		    ok=0; \
112		    for i in $$(seq 1 100); do \
113		        if ! kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null; then \
114		            echo "error: harness process (pid $$pid) exited during startup" >&2; \
115		            echo "--- $$log ---"; cat $$log 2>/dev/null; exit 1; \
116		        fi; \
117		        if lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$$pid"; then ok=1; break; fi; \
118		        sleep 0.1; \
119		    done; \
120		    if [ $$ok -ne 1 ]; then \
121		        echo "error: pid $$pid is not listening on 127.0.0.1:$$port after 10s" >&2; \
122		        echo "--- $$log ---"; cat $$log 2>/dev/null; exit 1; \
123		    fi; \
124		done
125		@echo "::: harness up — dashboard :$(DASH_PORT), proxy :$(PROXY_PORT)$(if $(BLACKHOLE_FLAG), (BLACKHOLE),) :::"
126	
127	.PHONY: harness-down
128	harness-down:  ## Stop the fake dashboard + stub proxy
129		@# Wait for each process to actually exit before dropping its pidfile:
130		@# harness-up runs this and then checks the ports, and a process still
131		@# on its way out would look like a stray and block the start (M2 review).
132		@for f in $(PROXY_PID) $(DASH_PID); do \
133		    if [ -f $$f ]; then \
134		        pid=$$(cat $$f); kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
135		        for i in $$(seq 1 50); do kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; \
136		        rm -f $$f; \
137		    fi; \
138		done
139		@echo "::: harness down :::"
140	
141	.PHONY: harness-reap
142	harness-reap:  ## Stop strays on the harness ports, pidfile or not
143		@# Two independent ways to confirm a listener is ours before killing it,
144		@# so this can never take out an unrelated service that happened to pick
145		@# the same port:
146		@#
147		@#   1. its command line names one of this directory's two scripts;
148		@#   2. its working directory IS this directory.
149		@#
150		@# Both are checked because `ps` is unavailable in some sandboxed shells
151		@# (it fails with "operation not permitted"), and a reaper that silently
152		@# declines to reap is a reaper that does not work when you need it.
153		@# `lsof` reports cwd in those same shells, so (2) is the one that holds.
154		@for port in $(DASH_PORT) $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) $(PROXY_PORT) $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT) $(GW_PORT) $(GW_CONTROL_PORT); do \
155		    for pid in $$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); do \
156		        cmd=$$(ps -o command= -p $$pid 2>/dev/null || true); \
157		        cwd=$$(lsof -a -p $$pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^n//p' | head -1); \
158		        mine=0; \
159		        case "$$cmd" in *dashboard.py*|*socks5stub.py*|*fake_gateway.py*) mine=1;; esac; \
160		        [ "$$cwd" = "$(CURDIR)" ] && mine=1; \
161		        if [ $$mine -eq 1 ]; then \
162		            echo "reaping pid $$pid on :$$port"; kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
163		        else \
164		            echo "pid $$pid on :$$port is not a harness process; leaving it alone" >&2; \
165		            echo "  command: $${cmd:-<unreadable>}" >&2; \
166		            echo "  cwd:     $${cwd:-<unreadable>}" >&2; \
167		        fi; \
168		    done; \
169		done
170		@rm -f $(PROXY_PID) $(DASH_PID) $(GW_PID)
171		@echo "::: strays reaped :::"
172	
173	.PHONY: bundle
174	bundle:  ## Fetch the pinned KiroCrew wheel (a no-op when cached and intact)
175		@$(PY) fake_gateway.py --fetch
176	
177	.PHONY: gateway-up
178	gateway-up: certs gateway-down  ## Start the fake KiroCrew gateway (GW_EXPIRE_IN=seconds)
179		@mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)
180		@for port in $(GW_PORT) $(GW_CONTROL_PORT); do \
181		    if lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
182		        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is already in use (a stray? make harness-reap)" >&2; exit 1; \
183		    fi; \
184		done
185		@$(PY) fake_gateway.py --port $(GW_PORT) --control-port $(GW_CONTROL_PORT) \
186			--cert server.pem --key server.key --expire-in $(GW_EXPIRE_IN) \
187			> $(GW_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(GW_PID)
188		@pid=$$(cat $(GW_PID)); ok=0; \
189		for i in $$(seq 1 100); do \
190		    if ! kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null; then \
191		        echo "error: the fake gateway exited during startup:" >&2; cat $(GW_LOG) >&2; exit 1; \
192		    fi; \
193		    if lsof -nP -iTCP:$(GW_PORT) -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$$pid"; then ok=1; break; fi; \
194		    sleep 0.1; \
195		done; \
196		if [ $$ok -ne 1 ]; then echo "error: the fake gateway is not listening after 10s" >&2; cat $(GW_LOG) >&2; exit 1; fi
197		@echo "::: fake gateway up — https://gw.tail-scale.ts.net via the stub, :$(GW_PORT), control :$(GW_CONTROL_PORT) :::"
198	
199	.PHONY: gateway-down
200	gateway-down:  ## Stop the fake KiroCrew gateway
201		@if [ -f $(GW_PID) ]; then \
202		    pid=$$(cat $(GW_PID)); kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
203		    for i in $$(seq 1 50); do kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; \
204		    rm -f $(GW_PID); \
205		fi
206	
207	.PHONY: gateway-check
208	gateway-check: gateway-up  ## Host-side contract self-test of the fake gateway
209		@status=0; $(PY) gateway_check.py --port $(GW_PORT) --control-port $(GW_CONTROL_PORT) --ca ca.pem || status=$$?; \
210		$(MAKE) --no-print-directory gateway-down; exit $$status
211	
212	.PHONY: harness-status
213	harness-status:  ## Show what is running
214		@for f in $(DASH_PID) $(PROXY_PID); do \
215		    if [ -f $$f ] && kill -0 $$(cat $$f) 2>/dev/null; then \
216		        echo "running: $$f -> $$(cat $$f)"; \
217		    else \
218		        echo "stopped: $$f"; \
219		    fi; \
220		done
221	
222	.PHONY: check
223	check: harness-up  ## Self-test the harness host-side with curl (no simulator)
224		@# Negative checks are explicit `if ...; then exit 1; fi`, never `! cmd`:
225		@# POSIX tells `set -e` to ignore a command starting with `!`, so a
226		@# `! curl ...` that should fail the check can never fail it (M2 review).
227		@set -e; \
228		CTL=http://127.0.0.1:$(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT); DCTL=http://127.0.0.1:$(DASH_CONTROL_PORT); \
229		PX=REDACTED \
230		count() { curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['requests'].get('$$1', 0))"; }; \
231		echo "==> HTTPS GET through the proxy (the tailnet-name path)"; \
232		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; echo "    ok"; \
233		echo "==> a wrong proxy password is rejected"; \
234		if curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy REDACTED https://$(DASH_HOST)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
235		    echo "FAIL: a wrong password got through" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
236		echo "==> the journal (file and control port) recorded the CONNECT"; \
237		grep -q '"event": *"connect"' $(JOURNAL); curl -s $$CTL/journal | grep -q '"connect"'; echo "    ok"; \
238		echo "==> a client that connects and never speaks stalls nobody (tls_accept)"; \
239		$(PY) -c "import subprocess, sys; from tls_accept import with_silent_client; \
240		    r = with_silent_client($(DASH_PORT), lambda: subprocess.run(['curl', '-sS', '--fail', '--max-time', '5', \
241		        '--cacert', 'ca.pem', 'https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/'], capture_output=True)); sys.exit(r.returncode)" \
242		    || { echo "FAIL: a silent client stalled the fake dashboard" >&2; exit 1; }; echo "    ok"; \
243		echo "==> R10 positive control: a DIRECT load of dash.localtest.me succeeds"; \
244		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
245		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
246		test "$$(count dash.localtest.me)" -ge 1; echo "    ok (a leak to this origin WOULD succeed, so a leak is detectable)"; \
247		echo "==> R10 negative: blackholed proxy fails, dashboard sees ZERO requests"; \
248		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; curl -s -X POST "$$CTL/mode?blackhole=1" >/dev/null; \
249		if curl -sS --fail --max-time 10 --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
250		    echo "FAIL: a blackholed proxy let the load through" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
251		test "$$(count dash.localtest.me)" -eq 0; \
252		curl -s $$CTL/journal | grep -q '"blackhole": true'; echo "    ok"; \
253		curl -s -X POST "$$CTL/mode?blackhole=0" >/dev/null; \
254		echo "==> R10 stub-gone variant: a closed listener refuses at TCP level"; \
255		curl -s -X POST $$CTL/close >/dev/null; \
256		if curl -sS --fail --max-time 5 --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
257		    echo "FAIL: a closed proxy listener still served the load" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
258		curl -s -X POST $$CTL/open >/dev/null; \
259		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; echo "    ok (and it recovers on /open)"; \
260		echo "==> M6: a report is stamped with the time the server received it"; \
261		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
262		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"doc":"probe"}' \
263		    https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__report >/dev/null; \
264		curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json, sys, time; r = json.load(sys.stdin)['reports']['dash.localtest.me']; \
265		    assert abs(r['received_at'] - time.time()) < 5 and r['received_seq'] >= 1, r"; echo "    ok"; \
266		echo "==> F4 D10: /__mode?front=502 answers 5xx on a LIVE connection, from the control port"; \
267		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=502" | grep -q '"front": *502'; \
268		code=$$(curl -s -o /tmp/front502.body -w '%{http_code}' --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/); \
269		if [ "$$code" != "502" ]; then echo "FAIL: front=502 served $$code, not 502" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
270		if [ -s /tmp/front502.body ]; then echo "FAIL: the 502 carried a body; ReverseProxy sends none" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
271		curl -s $$DCTL/__state | grep -q '"front": *502'; \
272		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=0" >/dev/null; \
273		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
274		rm -f /tmp/front502.body; echo "    ok (and front=0 restores the page)"; \
275		echo "==> ...and a bad front value is refused rather than silently ignored"; \
276		code=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=200"); \
277		if [ "$$code" != "400" ]; then echo "FAIL: front=200 answered $$code, not 400" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
278		echo "==> F9 §6 / F15 §6: the inset and shell probes, their viewports, /__mode?root= and /__state's insets"; \
279		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-cover | grep -q 'content="width=device-width, viewport-fit=cover"'; \
280		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-plain | grep -q 'content="width=device-width"'; \
281		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-product | grep -q 'interactive-widget=resizes-content, viewport-fit=cover"'; \
282		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=cover" | grep -q '"root": *"cover"'; \
283		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "INSET PROBE cover"; \
284		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=shell" | grep -q '"root": *"shell"'; \
285		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "SHELL PROBE"; \
286		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=page" >/dev/null; \
287		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
288		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
289		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"shell","scrollTop":0}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report >/dev/null; \
290		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"cover","top":"62px"}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report >/dev/null; \
291		curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json, sys; r = json.load(sys.stdin)['insets']['cover']; assert r['top'] == '62px' and r['received_seq'] >= 1, r"; \
292		code=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"nope"}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report); \
293		if [ "$$code" != "400" ]; then echo "FAIL: an unknown probe answered $$code, not 400" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
294		echo "==> F6: the TLS handshake counter sees a connection by its SNI, and /__reset clears it"; \
295		hs() { curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['handshakes'].get('$$1', 0))"; }; \
296		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
297		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/healthz >/dev/null; \
298		if [ "$$(hs dash.localtest.me)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: a handshake with SNI dash.localtest.me was not counted" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
299		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
300		if [ "$$(hs dash.localtest.me)" -ne 0 ]; then echo "FAIL: /__reset left the handshake count" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
301		echo "==> F6: /single-origin, /__mode?root=single, and its /f6/ resources"; \
302		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/single-origin | grep -q "SINGLE ORIGIN"; \
303		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=single" | grep -q '"root": *"single"'; \
304		curl -s $$DCTL/__state | grep -q '"root": *"single"'; \
305		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "SINGLE ORIGIN"; \
306		curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=page" >/dev/null; \
307		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
308		loc=$$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/f6/redirect-img); \
309		if [ "$$loc" != "302 https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/f6/redirected.png" ]; then \
310		    echo "FAIL: /f6/redirect-img answered '$$loc', not a 302 to the away origin" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
311		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/f6/inner | grep -q "https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/f6/inner-img.png"; \
312		curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
313		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://esm.sh/f6/cdn.js | grep -q "__F6_CDN"; \
314		if [ "$$(count esm.sh)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: esm.sh's request was not counted under its Host" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
315		echo "==> F6: a lookalike CDN host WOULD be served and counted (the anchoring test's positive control)"; \
316		curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://esm.sh.away.example/f6/pwn.js >/dev/null; \
317		if [ "$$(count esm.sh.away.example)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: esm.sh.away.example was not counted" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
318		echo "==> M6: /__ws_push reaches an open WebSocket and /__drop_ws cuts it, as a gateway restart does"; \
319		$(PY) -c "from dashboard import ws_drop_probe; ws_drop_probe($(DASH_PORT), $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT), 'ca.pem')"; echo "    ok"; \
320		echo "==> M6.4: the page reconnects as KiroCrew's does (1 s doubling to 10 s, reset on open, refetch)"; \
321		command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "FAIL: node is needed for page_check.js (brew install node)" >&2; exit 1; }; \
322		node page_check.js

file.content:
# Offline test harness: a stub SOCKS5 proxy in front of a fake dashboard.
#
# Runs with no Tailscale account, no tailnet and no network. The point is to
# exercise the WKWebView -> SOCKS5 -> HTTPS -> WebSocket/SSE path -- and the
# anti-leak negative case -- deterministically and in seconds.
#
#   make harness-up      start both, write pidfiles, wait until listening
#   make harness-down    stop both
#   make harness-status  what is running
#   make certs           mint the test CA + leaf (idempotent)
#   make trust           teach the booted simulator to trust the test CA
#   make bundle          fetch the pinned KiroCrew wheel into .cache (verified)
#   make gateway-up      start the fake KiroCrew gateway (real pinned bundle, M4)
#   make gateway-down    stop it
#   make gateway-check   its host-side contract self-test (starts and stops it)
#
# The fake gateway is separate from harness-up on purpose: it refuses to start
# unless its bundle is the pinned one, and a missing or wrong bundle must not
# take the offline (L1) suite down with it.
#
# BLACKHOLE=1 starts the proxy in refuse-every-CONNECT mode, which is the
# negative fixture: the page load must FAIL rather than quietly succeeding by
# some direct route.

PY           ?= python3
PROXY_PORT   ?= 1080
PROXY_CONTROL_PORT ?= 1081
DASH_PORT    ?= 8443
DASH_CONTROL_PORT  ?= 8480
GW_PORT      ?= 8444
GW_CONTROL_PORT ?= 8481
GW_EXPIRE_IN ?= 0
PROXY_USER   ?= tsnet
PROXY_PASS   ?= s3cret
DASH_HOST    ?= dash.tail-scale.ts.net
RUN_DIR      ?= .run
JOURNAL      ?= $(RUN_DIR)/proxy.ndjson
BLACKHOLE    ?= 0

PROXY_PID    := $(RUN_DIR)/socks5.pid
DASH_PID     := $(RUN_DIR)/dashboard.pid
PROXY_LOG    := $(RUN_DIR)/socks5.log
DASH_LOG     := $(RUN_DIR)/dashboard.log
GW_PID       := $(RUN_DIR)/gateway.pid
GW_LOG       := $(RUN_DIR)/gateway.log

# F6 §6: the hosts /single-origin reaches for besides the away origin. Under
# -ProxyEverything each would be SERVED -- and counted by Host -- by the fake
# dashboard if the app's rule list allowed it, and none can reach the real
# host. dash.tail-scale.ts.net:8444 is the port probe (a gateway rule that
# forgot the port); it is a map key, unrelated to GW_PORT's listener.
F6_MAPS := $(foreach hp,dash.tail-scale.ts.net:8444 esm.sh:443 esm.sh.away.example:443 \
             esm.shady.example:443 esm.sh:8444 fonts.googleapis.com:443 fonts.gstatic.com:443, \
             --map $(hp)=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT))

ifeq ($(BLACKHOLE),1)
  BLACKHOLE_FLAG := --blackhole
else
  BLACKHOLE_FLAG :=
endif

.PHONY: certs
certs:  ## Mint the test CA and leaf (no-op if present and unexpired)
	@./gen-certs.sh

.PHONY: trust
trust: certs  ## Trust the test CA in the booted simulator
	@xcrun simctl keychain booted add-root-cert "$(CURDIR)/ca.der"
	@echo "::: test CA trusted in the booted simulator :::"

.PHONY: harness-up
harness-up: certs harness-down  ## Start the fake dashboard + stub proxy
	@mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)
	@# Refuse to start on top of someone else's listener.
	@#
	@# This is not hypothetical: a dashboard left over from an earlier session
	@# was still holding :$(DASH_PORT), serving a certificate minted before the
	@# current CA. The replacement died instantly on "address already in use",
	@# a port probe saw the STRANGER still listening and reported the harness
	@# healthy, and every TLS check then failed with "unable to get local
	@# issuer certificate" -- which reads like a certificate bug and is not.
	@for port in $(DASH_PORT) $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) $(PROXY_PORT) $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT); do \
	    pids=$$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); \
	    if [ -n "$$pids" ]; then \
	        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is already in use by pid(s): $$pids" >&2; \
	        echo "       These are probably strays from an earlier run." >&2; \
	        echo "       Stop them with: make harness-reap" >&2; \
	        exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@# Truncate the journal so an assertion can't pass on a previous run's
	@# connect events -- the exact way this kind of test rots into a no-op.
	@: > $(JOURNAL)
	@$(PY) dashboard.py --port $(DASH_PORT) --control-port $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) \
		--cert server.pem --key server.key > $(DASH_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(DASH_PID)
	@$(PY) socks5stub.py --port $(PROXY_PORT) \
		--user $(PROXY_USER) --password $(PROXY_PASS) \
		--journal $(JOURNAL) $(BLACKHOLE_FLAG) --control-port $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT) \
		--map $(DASH_HOST):443=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) \
		--map wrong.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) \
		--map down.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:9 \
		--map gw.tail-scale.ts.net:443=127.0.0.1:$(GW_PORT) \
		$(F6_MAPS) \
		> $(PROXY_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(PROXY_PID)
	@# Wait for OUR processes to listen. Checking the port alone is what let
	@# the stray above masquerade as a healthy harness, so verify the pid we
	@# started is both alive and the one holding the port.
	@for spec in "$(DASH_PORT):$(DASH_PID):$(DASH_LOG)" "$(PROXY_PORT):$(PROXY_PID):$(PROXY_LOG)"; do \
	    port=$${spec%%:*}; rest=$${spec#*:}; pidfile=$${rest%%:*}; log=$${rest#*:}; \
	    pid=$$(cat $$pidfile); \
	    ok=0; \
	    for i in $$(seq 1 100); do \
	        if ! kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null; then \
	            echo "error: harness process (pid $$pid) exited during startup" >&2; \
	            echo "--- $$log ---"; cat $$log 2>/dev/null; exit 1; \
	        fi; \
	        if lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$$pid"; then ok=1; break; fi; \
	        sleep 0.1; \
	    done; \
	    if [ $$ok -ne 1 ]; then \
	        echo "error: pid $$pid is not listening on 127.0.0.1:$$port after 10s" >&2; \
	        echo "--- $$log ---"; cat $$log 2>/dev/null; exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@echo "::: harness up — dashboard :$(DASH_PORT), proxy :$(PROXY_PORT)$(if $(BLACKHOLE_FLAG), (BLACKHOLE),) :::"

.PHONY: harness-down
harness-down:  ## Stop the fake dashboard + stub proxy
	@# Wait for each process to actually exit before dropping its pidfile:
	@# harness-up runs this and then checks the ports, and a process still
	@# on its way out would look like a stray and block the start (M2 review).
	@for f in $(PROXY_PID) $(DASH_PID); do \
	    if [ -f $$f ]; then \
	        pid=$$(cat $$f); kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
	        for i in $$(seq 1 50); do kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; \
	        rm -f $$f; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@echo "::: harness down :::"

.PHONY: harness-reap
harness-reap:  ## Stop strays on the harness ports, pidfile or not
	@# Two independent ways to confirm a listener is ours before killing it,
	@# so this can never take out an unrelated service that happened to pick
	@# the same port:
	@#
	@#   1. its command line names one of this directory's two scripts;
	@#   2. its working directory IS this directory.
	@#
	@# Both are checked because `ps` is unavailable in some sandboxed shells
	@# (it fails with "operation not permitted"), and a reaper that silently
	@# declines to reap is a reaper that does not work when you need it.
	@# `lsof` reports cwd in those same shells, so (2) is the one that holds.
	@for port in $(DASH_PORT) $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT) $(PROXY_PORT) $(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT) $(GW_PORT) $(GW_CONTROL_PORT); do \
	    for pid in $$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); do \
	        cmd=$$(ps -o command= -p $$pid 2>/dev/null || true); \
	        cwd=$$(lsof -a -p $$pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^n//p' | head -1); \
	        mine=0; \
	        case "$$cmd" in *dashboard.py*|*socks5stub.py*|*fake_gateway.py*) mine=1;; esac; \
	        [ "$$cwd" = "$(CURDIR)" ] && mine=1; \
	        if [ $$mine -eq 1 ]; then \
	            echo "reaping pid $$pid on :$$port"; kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
	        else \
	            echo "pid $$pid on :$$port is not a harness process; leaving it alone" >&2; \
	            echo "  command: $${cmd:-<unreadable>}" >&2; \
	            echo "  cwd:     $${cwd:-<unreadable>}" >&2; \
	        fi; \
	    done; \
	done
	@rm -f $(PROXY_PID) $(DASH_PID) $(GW_PID)
	@echo "::: strays reaped :::"

.PHONY: bundle
bundle:  ## Fetch the pinned KiroCrew wheel (a no-op when cached and intact)
	@$(PY) fake_gateway.py --fetch

.PHONY: gateway-up
gateway-up: certs gateway-down  ## Start the fake KiroCrew gateway (GW_EXPIRE_IN=seconds)
	@mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)
	@for port in $(GW_PORT) $(GW_CONTROL_PORT); do \
	    if lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is already in use (a stray? make harness-reap)" >&2; exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@$(PY) fake_gateway.py --port $(GW_PORT) --control-port $(GW_CONTROL_PORT) \
		--cert server.pem --key server.key --expire-in $(GW_EXPIRE_IN) \
		> $(GW_LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(GW_PID)
	@pid=$$(cat $(GW_PID)); ok=0; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 100); do \
	    if ! kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null; then \
	        echo "error: the fake gateway exited during startup:" >&2; cat $(GW_LOG) >&2; exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	    if lsof -nP -iTCP:$(GW_PORT) -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$$pid"; then ok=1; break; fi; \
	    sleep 0.1; \
	done; \
	if [ $$ok -ne 1 ]; then echo "error: the fake gateway is not listening after 10s" >&2; cat $(GW_LOG) >&2; exit 1; fi
	@echo "::: fake gateway up — https://gw.tail-scale.ts.net via the stub, :$(GW_PORT), control :$(GW_CONTROL_PORT) :::"

.PHONY: gateway-down
gateway-down:  ## Stop the fake KiroCrew gateway
	@if [ -f $(GW_PID) ]; then \
	    pid=$$(cat $(GW_PID)); kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
	    for i in $$(seq 1 50); do kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; \
	    rm -f $(GW_PID); \
	fi

.PHONY: gateway-check
gateway-check: gateway-up  ## Host-side contract self-test of the fake gateway
	@status=0; $(PY) gateway_check.py --port $(GW_PORT) --control-port $(GW_CONTROL_PORT) --ca ca.pem || status=$$?; \
	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory gateway-down; exit $$status

.PHONY: harness-status
harness-status:  ## Show what is running
	@for f in $(DASH_PID) $(PROXY_PID); do \
	    if [ -f $$f ] && kill -0 $$(cat $$f) 2>/dev/null; then \
	        echo "running: $$f -> $$(cat $$f)"; \
	    else \
	        echo "stopped: $$f"; \
	    fi; \
	done

.PHONY: check
check: harness-up  ## Self-test the harness host-side with curl (no simulator)
	@# Negative checks are explicit `if ...; then exit 1; fi`, never `! cmd`:
	@# POSIX tells `set -e` to ignore a command starting with `!`, so a
	@# `! curl ...` that should fail the check can never fail it (M2 review).
	@set -e; \
	CTL=http://127.0.0.1:$(PROXY_CONTROL_PORT); DCTL=http://127.0.0.1:$(DASH_CONTROL_PORT); \
	PX=REDACTED \
	count() { curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['requests'].get('$$1', 0))"; }; \
	echo "==> HTTPS GET through the proxy (the tailnet-name path)"; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> a wrong proxy password is rejected"; \
	if curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy REDACTED https://$(DASH_HOST)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "FAIL: a wrong password got through" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> the journal (file and control port) recorded the CONNECT"; \
	grep -q '"event": *"connect"' $(JOURNAL); curl -s $$CTL/journal | grep -q '"connect"'; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> a client that connects and never speaks stalls nobody (tls_accept)"; \
	$(PY) -c "import subprocess, sys; from tls_accept import with_silent_client; \
	    r = with_silent_client($(DASH_PORT), lambda: subprocess.run(['curl', '-sS', '--fail', '--max-time', '5', \
	        '--cacert', 'ca.pem', 'https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/'], capture_output=True)); sys.exit(r.returncode)" \
	    || { echo "FAIL: a silent client stalled the fake dashboard" >&2; exit 1; }; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> R10 positive control: a DIRECT load of dash.localtest.me succeeds"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
	test "$$(count dash.localtest.me)" -ge 1; echo "    ok (a leak to this origin WOULD succeed, so a leak is detectable)"; \
	echo "==> R10 negative: blackholed proxy fails, dashboard sees ZERO requests"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; curl -s -X POST "$$CTL/mode?blackhole=1" >/dev/null; \
	if curl -sS --fail --max-time 10 --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "FAIL: a blackholed proxy let the load through" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	test "$$(count dash.localtest.me)" -eq 0; \
	curl -s $$CTL/journal | grep -q '"blackhole": true'; echo "    ok"; \
	curl -s -X POST "$$CTL/mode?blackhole=0" >/dev/null; \
	echo "==> R10 stub-gone variant: a closed listener refuses at TCP level"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$CTL/close >/dev/null; \
	if curl -sS --fail --max-time 5 --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    echo "FAIL: a closed proxy listener still served the load" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	curl -s -X POST $$CTL/open >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; echo "    ok (and it recovers on /open)"; \
	echo "==> M6: a report is stamped with the time the server received it"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"doc":"probe"}' \
	    https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__report >/dev/null; \
	curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json, sys, time; r = json.load(sys.stdin)['reports']['dash.localtest.me']; \
	    assert abs(r['received_at'] - time.time()) < 5 and r['received_seq'] >= 1, r"; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> F4 D10: /__mode?front=502 answers 5xx on a LIVE connection, from the control port"; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=502" | grep -q '"front": *502'; \
	code=$$(curl -s -o /tmp/front502.body -w '%{http_code}' --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/); \
	if [ "$$code" != "502" ]; then echo "FAIL: front=502 served $$code, not 502" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	if [ -s /tmp/front502.body ]; then echo "FAIL: the 502 carried a body; ReverseProxy sends none" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	curl -s $$DCTL/__state | grep -q '"front": *502'; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=0" >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
	rm -f /tmp/front502.body; echo "    ok (and front=0 restores the page)"; \
	echo "==> ...and a bad front value is refused rather than silently ignored"; \
	code=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?front=200"); \
	if [ "$$code" != "400" ]; then echo "FAIL: front=200 answered $$code, not 400" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> F9 §6 / F15 §6: the inset and shell probes, their viewports, /__mode?root= and /__state's insets"; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-cover | grep -q 'content="width=device-width, viewport-fit=cover"'; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-plain | grep -q 'content="width=device-width"'; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/__inset-product | grep -q 'interactive-widget=resizes-content, viewport-fit=cover"'; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=cover" | grep -q '"root": *"cover"'; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "INSET PROBE cover"; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=shell" | grep -q '"root": *"shell"'; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "SHELL PROBE"; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=page" >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"shell","scrollTop":0}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"cover","top":"62px"}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report >/dev/null; \
	curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json, sys; r = json.load(sys.stdin)['insets']['cover']; assert r['top'] == '62px' and r['received_seq'] >= 1, r"; \
	code=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --cacert ca.pem -d '{"probe":"nope"}' https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/__inset-report); \
	if [ "$$code" != "400" ]; then echo "FAIL: an unknown probe answered $$code, not 400" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> F6: the TLS handshake counter sees a connection by its SNI, and /__reset clears it"; \
	hs() { curl -s $$DCTL/__state | $(PY) -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['handshakes'].get('$$1', 0))"; }; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/healthz >/dev/null; \
	if [ "$$(hs dash.localtest.me)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: a handshake with SNI dash.localtest.me was not counted" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	if [ "$$(hs dash.localtest.me)" -ne 0 ]; then echo "FAIL: /__reset left the handshake count" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> F6: /single-origin, /__mode?root=single, and its /f6/ resources"; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/single-origin | grep -q "SINGLE ORIGIN"; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=single" | grep -q '"root": *"single"'; \
	curl -s $$DCTL/__state | grep -q '"root": *"single"'; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "SINGLE ORIGIN"; \
	curl -sS --fail -X POST "$$DCTL/__mode?root=page" >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/ | grep -q "FAKE DASHBOARD"; \
	loc=$$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/f6/redirect-img); \
	if [ "$$loc" != "302 https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/f6/redirected.png" ]; then \
	    echo "FAIL: /f6/redirect-img answered '$$loc', not a 302 to the away origin" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://$(DASH_HOST)/f6/inner | grep -q "https://dash.localtest.me:$(DASH_PORT)/f6/inner-img.png"; \
	curl -s -X POST $$DCTL/__reset >/dev/null; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://esm.sh/f6/cdn.js | grep -q "__F6_CDN"; \
	if [ "$$(count esm.sh)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: esm.sh's request was not counted under its Host" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> F6: a lookalike CDN host WOULD be served and counted (the anchoring test's positive control)"; \
	curl -sS --fail --cacert ca.pem --proxy $$PX https://esm.sh.away.example/f6/pwn.js >/dev/null; \
	if [ "$$(count esm.sh.away.example)" -lt 1 ]; then echo "FAIL: esm.sh.away.example was not counted" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> M6: /__ws_push reaches an open WebSocket and /__drop_ws cuts it, as a gateway restart does"; \
	$(PY) -c "from dashboard import ws_drop_probe; ws_drop_probe($(DASH_PORT), $(DASH_CONTROL_PORT), 'ca.pem')"; echo "    ok"; \
	echo "==> M6.4: the page reconnects as KiroCrew's does (1 s doubling to 10 s, reset on open, refetch)"; \
	command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "FAIL: node is needed for page_check.js (brew install node)" >&2; exit 1; }; \
	node page_check.js
	@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory harness-down

.PHONY: help
help:  ## Show this help
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*##"} /^[a-zA-Z_-][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:.*##/ {printf "  \033[36m%-16s\033[0m %s\n", $$1, $$2}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

# L2 harness: a fake Tailscale control plane with real tsnet peers (PLAN M3,
# revision R17). The app's real embedded node joins it from the simulator,
# which shares this host's loopback.
#
#   make build   build the harness (the app's vendored tailscale, R16)
#   make up      start the fake dashboard (../harness) and this harness
#   make down    stop both
#   make reap    stop strays on this harness's ports
#   make check   host-side self-test, no simulator (~10 s)
#
# Ports: the control plane on 127.0.0.1:8490 (the app's -TestControlURL) and
# the test API on 127.0.0.1:8491. The dash peer forwards to the fake dashboard
# on 127.0.0.1:8443, which `up` starts through ../harness.

CONTROL_PORT ?= 8490
API_PORT     ?= 8491
DASH_PORT    ?= 8443
RUN_DIR      ?= .run
# Extra harness flags, e.g. HARNESS_ARGS="-gateway 127.0.0.1:8444 -slow-peer"
# for the discovery suite (M5). Plain `=`: only the make command line can set
# it, never an exported environment variable (M5 review).
HARNESS_ARGS =
BIN          := $(RUN_DIR)/tsnet-harness
PID          := $(RUN_DIR)/tsnet-harness.pid
LOG          := $(RUN_DIR)/tsnet-harness.log
STATE        := $(CURDIR)/$(RUN_DIR)/state
CHECK_STATE  := $(CURDIR)/$(RUN_DIR)/check-state

.PHONY: build
build:  ## Build the harness
	@mkdir -p $(RUN_DIR)
	@go build -o $(BIN) .

.PHONY: up
up: build down  ## Start the fake dashboard and the harness
	@$(MAKE) -C ../harness --no-print-directory harness-up
	@for port in $(CONTROL_PORT) $(API_PORT); do \
	    pids=$$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); \
	    if [ -n "$$pids" ]; then \
	        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is already in use by pid(s): $$pids" >&2; \
	        echo "       Probably a stray from an earlier run: make reap" >&2; \
	        exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@rm -rf $(STATE)
	@$(BIN) -control 127.0.0.1:$(CONTROL_PORT) -api 127.0.0.1:$(API_PORT) \
	    -dashboard 127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) -state $(STATE) $(HARNESS_ARGS) > $(LOG) 2>&1 & echo $$! > $(PID)
	@# Ready means OUR process answers /healthz: the first reset (peers up)
	@# has completed. A port probe alone would accept a stray (see ../harness).
	@pid=$$(cat $(PID)); ok=0; \
	for i in $$(seq 1 300); do \
	    if ! kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null; then \
	        echo "error: tsnet-harness (pid $$pid) exited during startup" >&2; cat $(LOG); exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	    if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:$(API_PORT)/healthz >/dev/null 2>&1 \
	        && lsof -nP -iTCP:$(API_PORT) -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$$pid"; then ok=1; break; fi; \
	    sleep 0.1; \
	done; \
	if [ $$ok -ne 1 ]; then echo "error: tsnet-harness not ready after 30s" >&2; cat $(LOG); exit 1; fi
	@echo "::: tsnet harness up — control http://127.0.0.1:$(CONTROL_PORT), api :$(API_PORT) :::"

.PHONY: down
down:  ## Stop the harness and the fake dashboard
	@# Kill the pid only if it is still ours (its cwd is this directory): a
	@# harness that died leaves its pidfile behind, and the number may since
	@# belong to something else (M3 review).
	@if [ -f $(PID) ]; then \
	    pid=$$(cat $(PID)); \
	    cwd=$$(lsof -a -p $$pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^n//p' | head -1); \
	    if [ "$$cwd" = "$(CURDIR)" ]; then \
	        kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
	        for i in $$(seq 1 50); do kill -0 $$pid 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; \
	    fi; \
	    rm -f $(PID); \
	fi
	@$(MAKE) -C ../harness --no-print-directory harness-down >/dev/null
	@echo "::: tsnet harness down :::"

.PHONY: reap
reap:  ## Stop strays on the harness ports (only processes run from here)
	@for port in $(CONTROL_PORT) $(API_PORT); do \
	    for pid in $$(lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t 2>/dev/null || true); do \
	        cwd=$$(lsof -a -p $$pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^n//p' | head -1); \
	        if [ "$$cwd" = "$(CURDIR)" ]; then \
	            echo "reaping pid $$pid on :$$port"; kill $$pid 2>/dev/null || true; \
	        else \
	            echo "pid $$pid on :$$port is not ours (cwd $${cwd:-<unreadable>}); leaving it" >&2; \
	        fi; \
	    done; \
	done
	@rm -f $(PID)
	@$(MAKE) -C ../harness --no-print-directory harness-reap

.PHONY: check
check: build  ## Host-side self-test (needs the fake dashboard; starts and stops it)
	@# Refuse to run over a live harness: this starts and stops the shared
	@# fake dashboard and needs the same ports (M3 review).
	@if [ -f $(PID) ] && kill -0 $$(cat $(PID)) 2>/dev/null; then \
	    echo "error: the harness is running (make up); stop it first with make down" >&2; exit 1; \
	fi
	@for port in $(CONTROL_PORT) $(API_PORT); do \
	    if lsof -nP -iTCP:$$port -sTCP:LISTEN -t >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	        echo "error: 127.0.0.1:$$port is in use; a stray? make reap" >&2; exit 1; \
	    fi; \
	done
	@$(MAKE) -C ../harness --no-print-directory harness-up
	@status=0; \
	$(BIN) -selftest -ca ../harness/ca.pem -control 127.0.0.1:$(CONTROL_PORT) \
	    -api 127.0.0.1:$(API_PORT) -dashboard 127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) -state $(CHECK_STATE) \
	    -gateway 127.0.0.1:$(DASH_PORT) -slow-peer || status=$$?; \
	$(MAKE) -C ../harness --no-print-directory harness-down >/dev/null; \
	rm -rf $(CHECK_STATE); \
	exit $$status

.PHONY: help
help:  ## Show this help
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*##"} /^[a-zA-Z_-][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:.*##/ {printf "  \033[36m%-10s\033[0m %s\n", $$1, $$2}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

240	    xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot "$LOG_DIR/failure.png" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
241	    cp "$HARNESS/.run/"*.log "$LOG_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || true

244	fi
245	# 240s, up from M2's 180s: F4 added three tests, one of which deliberately
246	# stalls a dial for 22 s (and WebKit's own second dial takes it to ~39 s) --
247	# there is no shorter way to hold a connecting state long enough to assert
248	# anything about it. A budget that is always exceeded stops being read, so it
249	# moved rather than being left to warn on every green run.
250	say "passed in ${ELAPSED}s (budget: 240s)"
251	if [[ $ELAPSED -gt 240 ]]; then
252	    say "WARNING: over the budget of 4 minutes"
253	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#

#   7. teardown    stop the harness, whatever happened

# it, the last test build is reused, which is what the < 4 min budget assumes.
#
# On failure: a screenshot and the harness logs are left under
# app/build/offline-logs/<timestamp>/.
set -euo pipefail

APP="$ROOT/app"
HARNESS="$ROOT/testing/harness"
SIM_NAME="${SIM_NAME:-iPhone 17}"
BUNDLE="net.lixom.latchkey"
BUILD=0

START=$(date +%s)
say() { printf '::: %s\n' "$*"; }

# The check allow-lists the fixture tailnets rather than naming one real one,
# so it protects every checkout and not just its author's.

    "$APP/UITests/OfflineHarnessTests.swift" "$HARNESS"/*.py \

    say "         Accepted (decision D7): the tests use no tailnet names or addresses,"
    say "         but leak coverage for tailnet *IP* destinations is limited on this host."

say "certs"
make -C "$HARNESS" --no-print-directory certs >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- simulator --
say "simulator: $SIM_NAME"
UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j | python3 -c "
import json, sys
for devs in json.load(sys.stdin)['devices'].values():
    for d in devs:
        if d['name'] == '$SIM_NAME':
            print(d['udid']); sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)") || { echo "error: no simulator named $SIM_NAME" >&2; exit 1; }

# wrote. Other suites (M4's session tests serve the real KiroCrew bundle,
# whose cached JS contains `?token=` in code) share the container otherwise.
# test-without-building installs the app again.
xcrun simctl uninstall "$UDID" "$BUNDLE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ harness --
teardown() {
    make -C "$HARNESS" --no-print-directory harness-down >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# lean on -- that a blackholed CONNECT fails and a direct load of the leak
# origin succeeds (R10's positive control), that a silent client stalls

        -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData LATCHKEY_GIT_SHA="$GIT_SHA" \
        "${SANDBOX_FLAGS[@]}" > "$LOG_DIR/build.log" 2>&1) \
        || { echo "error: build failed; see $LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- tests --
# Two passes. The sign-in test runs LAST and alone, so R1's disk scan below
# sees the state it left: every other test launches with
# -UITestResetWorkspaces, which deletes the workspace data, and XCTest runs
# tests alphabetically, so a later test would erase the evidence (M2 review).
SIGNIN="LatchkeyUITests/OfflineHarnessTests/testSignInTokenIsStrippedFromTheAddress"
run_tests() {   # $1 = label, rest = -only-testing/-skip-testing args
    local label=$1; shift
    (cd "$APP" && xcodebuild test-without-building -project Latchkey.xcodeproj -scheme Latchkey \
        -configuration Testing -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" \
        -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData -resultBundlePath "$LOG_DIR/$label.xcresult" \
        -parallel-testing-enabled NO -test-timeouts-enabled YES \
        -default-test-execution-time-allowance 120 "$@") > "$LOG_DIR/$label.log" 2>&1
}
say "OfflineHarnessTests"
set +e
run_tests suite -only-testing:LatchkeyUITests/OfflineHarnessTests -skip-testing:"$SIGNIN"
SUITE_RC=$?
run_tests signin -only-testing:"$SIGNIN"
SIGNIN_RC=$?
set -e
TEST_RC=$(( SUITE_RC | SIGNIN_RC ))
cat "$LOG_DIR/suite.log" "$LOG_DIR/signin.log" > "$LOG_DIR/test.log"
grep -E "Test Case .*(passed|failed)" "$LOG_DIR/test.log" | sed 's/^/    /' || true
# Both passes together must pass every test in the file: a stale build or a
# wrong name runs nothing and still exits 0 (M3 review).
PASSED=$(grep -cE "Test Case .*OfflineHarnessTests.* passed" "$LOG_DIR/test.log" || true)
if [[ $TEST_RC -eq 0 && "$PASSED" -ne "$EXPECTED" ]]; then
    echo "error: $PASSED of $EXPECTED OfflineHarnessTests passed (a stale build? try --build)" >&2
    TEST_RC=1
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- R1 check --
# testSignInTokenIsStrippedFromTheAddress loads /?token=OFFLINE-TEST-TOKEN-7f3a
# through the real app, so after the suite a token has genuinely passed
# through. Nothing written by the app may contain it, or any `token=`.
say "R1: no sign-in token in the app container's logs"
CONTAINER=$(xcrun simctl get_app_container "$UDID" "$BUNDLE" data 2>/dev/null || true)
LEAK_RC=0
# grep exits 0 on a match, 1 on none and 2 on an error -- and `if grep ...;
# then leak; else ok` read 1 and 2 alike as ok, so an unreadable file or a
# missing directory printed "ok" over a real hit (review, 2026-09-23: grep
# returns 2 even when it also matched). scan keeps the three apart: matches
# go to the named file, errors are shown, and the status is grep's own.
scan() {  # outfile, grep args...
    local out=$1 rc=0; shift
    grep "$@" > "$out" 2> "$out.err" || rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -ge 2 ]]; then
        echo "error: the scan could not read everything it was asked to (grep exit $rc):" >&2
        sed 's/^/    /' "$out.err" | head -5 >&2
    fi
    return $rc
}
if [[ -n "$CONTAINER" ]]; then
    # Everything the app can write: all of Library (Application Support,
    # WebKit's website data and caches, Cookies, HTTPStorages, Preferences)
    # and tmp. -a so binary stores (SQLite, the HTTP cache) are searched too;
    # the page no longer carries the token as a literal, so a hit is real.
    SCAN_RC=0
    scan "$LOG_DIR/token-leaks.txt" -rla -e "OFFLINE-TEST-TOKEN" -e "token=" \
        "$CONTAINER/Library" "$CONTAINER/tmp" || SCAN_RC=$?
    if [[ -s "$LOG_DIR/token-leaks.txt" ]]; then
        echo "error: a sign-in token was written to disk:" >&2
        sed "s|$CONTAINER/|    |" "$LOG_DIR/token-leaks.txt" >&2
        LEAK_RC=1
    fi
    if [[ $SCAN_RC -ge 2 ]]; then
        echo "error: the disk scan is incomplete, so 'no token on disk' is not established" >&2
        LEAK_RC=1
    elif [[ $SCAN_RC -eq 1 ]]; then
        # Not vacuous only if the sign-in run left WebKit data to search.
        WK_FILES=$(find "$CONTAINER/Library/WebKit" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
        if [[ "$WK_FILES" -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "error: no WebKit data on disk after the sign-in test, so the disk scan" >&2
            echo "       searched nothing. Did the sign-in test run last?" >&2
            LEAK_RC=1
        else
            echo "    ok (disk: all of Library + tmp, $WK_FILES WebKit files among them)"
        fi
    fi
    # The unified log is the other place the app writes. Scan this run's.
    xcrun simctl spawn "$UDID" log show --last "$(( $(date +%s) - START + 30 ))s" \
        --predicate "subsystem == \"$BUNDLE\"" --style compact > "$LOG_DIR/unified.log" 2>/dev/null || true
    SCAN_RC=0
    scan "$LOG_DIR/token-in-os-log.txt" -e "OFFLINE-TEST-TOKEN" -e "token=" "$LOG_DIR/unified.log" || SCAN_RC=$?
    if [[ -s "$LOG_DIR/token-in-os-log.txt" ]]; then
        echo "error: a sign-in token reached the unified log:" >&2
        sed 's/^/    /' "$LOG_DIR/token-in-os-log.txt" | head -5 >&2
        LEAK_RC=1
    fi
    if [[ $SCAN_RC -ge 2 ]]; then
        echo "error: the unified-log scan is incomplete" >&2
        LEAK_RC=1
    elif [[ $SCAN_RC -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "    ok (unified log: $(wc -l < "$LOG_DIR/unified.log" | tr -d ' ') lines scanned)"
    fi
    # Validate the instrument: a grep that finds nothing proves nothing unless
    # the token URL was actually logged. The sign-in test runs with
    # -UITestLogResponses, which logs every navigation URL, so its REDACTED
    # form must be present. If it is missing, the check above was vacuous.
    if grep -q 'RESP-LOG action: https://dash.tail-scale.ts.net/?…' "$LOG_DIR/unified.log"; then
        echo "    ok (validated: the sign-in URL was logged, in redacted form)"
    else
        echo "error: the redacted sign-in navigation is not in the log, so the token" >&2
        echo "       check proved nothing. Did testSignInTokenIsStrippedFromTheAddress run" >&2
        echo "       with -UITestLogResponses?" >&2
        LEAK_RC=1
    fi
else
    echo "    skipped: app container not found (was the app installed?)"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary --
ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))
if [[ $TEST_RC -ne 0 || $LEAK_RC -ne 0 ]]; then
    xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot "$LOG_DIR/failure.png" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    cp "$HARNESS/.run/"*.log "$LOG_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || true
    say "FAILED in ${ELAPSED}s — logs, screenshot and xcresult in $LOG_DIR"
    exit 1
fi
# 240s, up from M2's 180s: F4 added three tests, one of which deliberately
# stalls a dial for 22 s (and WebKit's own second dial takes it to ~39 s) --
# there is no shorter way to hold a connecting state long enough to assert
# anything about it. A budget that is always exceeded stops being read, so it
# moved rather than being left to warn on every green run.
say "passed in ${ELAPSED}s (budget: 240s)"
if [[ $ELAPSED -gt 240 ]]; then
    say "WARNING: over the budget of 4 minutes"
fi

205	    fi

207	        echo "error: the scan could not read everything it was asked to (grep exit $SCAN_RC):" >&2
208	        sed 's/^/    /' "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt.err" | head -5 >&2
209	        echo "error: the disk scan is incomplete, so 'no login link on disk' is not established" >&2
210	        TEST_RC=1
211	    elif [[ $SCAN_RC -eq 1 ]]; then
212	        if ! grep -rqa "/auth/…" "$CONTAINER/Library/Application Support/"*/Logs/tsnet.log* 2>/dev/null; then
213	            echo "error: no redacted login link in tsnet.log, so the scan proved nothing" >&2
214	            TEST_RC=1
215	        else
216	            echo "    ok (all of Library + tmp, searched for $LINK_COUNT minted link(s) literally; tsnet.log holds them redacted)"
217	        fi
218	    fi
219	fi
220	
221	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary --
222	ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))
223	if [[ $TEST_RC -ne 0 ]]; then
224	    xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot "$LOG_DIR/failure.png" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
225	    cp "$TSNET/.run/"*.log "$HARNESS/.run/"*.log "$LOG_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || true
226	    curl -s "$HARNESS_API/state" > "$LOG_DIR/harness-state.json" 2>/dev/null || true
227	    say "FAILED in ${ELAPSED}s — logs, screenshot and xcresult in $LOG_DIR"
228	    exit 1
229	fi
230	say "passed in ${ELAPSED}s (budget: 300s)"
231	if [[ $ELAPSED -gt 300 ]]; then
232	    say "WARNING: over the L2 budget of 5 minutes"
233	fi

SELFTEST_STAMP="$TSNET/.run/selftest.sha"
# HEAD:PATH resolves PATH from the repository ROOT whatever -C says, and app/
# stopped being its own repository on 2026-09-23; the leading ./ makes it
# relative to app/ wherever app/ sits. A hash this command could not compute
# is no basis for skipping anything, so its failure is fatal and says why
# rather than surfacing as a bare git error two lines into the preflight.
VENDORED_TREE=$(git -C "$APP" rev-parse "HEAD:./ThirdParty/libtailscale/tailscale-patched") \
    || { echo "error: cannot hash the vendored tailscale tree (git's message is above), so whether" >&2
         echo "       the harness self-test may be skipped is undecidable. Not guessing." >&2; exit 1; }
SELFTEST_HASH=$(cat "$TSNET"/*.go "$TSNET"/go.mod "$TSNET"/go.sum "$TSNET"/Makefile <(echo "$VENDORED_TREE") \
                | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [[ "${SELFTEST:-auto}" != always && -z "$(git -C "$APP" status --porcelain -- "$VENDORED")" \
      && -f "$SELFTEST_STAMP" && "$(cat "$SELFTEST_STAMP")" == "$SELFTEST_HASH" ]]; then
    say "tsnet harness self-test: skipped (unchanged since it last passed; SELFTEST=always forces it)"
else
    say "tsnet harness self-test"
    make -C "$TSNET" --no-print-directory check > "$LOG_DIR/selftest.log" 2>&1 \
        || { cat "$LOG_DIR/selftest.log" >&2; echo "error: the harness self-test failed" >&2; exit 1; }
    grep -E "^(==>|selftest)" "$LOG_DIR/selftest.log" | sed 's/^/    /'
    mkdir -p "$TSNET/.run" && echo "$SELFTEST_HASH" > "$SELFTEST_STAMP"
fi
say "harness up"
make -C "$TSNET" --no-print-directory up

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- simulator --
say "simulator: $SIM_NAME"
UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j | python3 -c "
import json, sys
for devs in json.load(sys.stdin)['devices'].values():
    for d in devs:
        if d['name'] == '$SIM_NAME':
            print(d['udid']); sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)") || { echo "error: no simulator named $SIM_NAME" >&2; exit 1; }
xcrun simctl bootstatus "$UDID" -b >/dev/null
xcrun simctl keychain "$UDID" add-root-cert "$HARNESS/ca.der"
# A fresh app container, so the login-link scan below reads only this run's.
xcrun simctl uninstall "$UDID" net.lixom.latchkey >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- build --
SANDBOX_FLAGS=()
if ! sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)' /usr/bin/true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SANDBOX_FLAGS=("OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS=\$(inherited) -disable-sandbox")
fi
if [[ $BUILD -eq 1 ]]; then
    # A vendored Go change is only in the app once the framework is rebuilt
    # (R29 shipped a stale one); a no-op when it is current.
    say "TailscaleKit framework (rebuilds only if libtailscale changed; minutes if so)"
    make -C "$APP" --no-print-directory framework > "$LOG_DIR/framework.log" 2>&1 \
        || { echo "error: TailscaleKit framework build failed; see $LOG_DIR/framework.log" >&2; exit 1; }
    say "build-for-testing (Testing configuration)"
    (cd "$APP" && xcodebuild build-for-testing -project Latchkey.xcodeproj -scheme Latchkey \
        -configuration Testing -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" \
        -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData "${SANDBOX_FLAGS[@]}" > "$LOG_DIR/build.log" 2>&1) \
        || { echo "error: build failed; see $LOG_DIR/build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- tests --
say "TailnetHarnessTests"
set +e
(cd "$APP" && xcodebuild test-without-building -project Latchkey.xcodeproj -scheme Latchkey \
    -configuration Testing -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" \
    -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData -resultBundlePath "$LOG_DIR/tests.xcresult" \
    -parallel-testing-enabled NO -test-timeouts-enabled YES \
    -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
    -only-testing:LatchkeyUITests/TailnetHarnessTests) > "$LOG_DIR/test.log" 2>&1
TEST_RC=$?
set -e
grep -E "Test Case .*(passed|failed)" "$LOG_DIR/test.log" | sed 's/^/    /' || true
# A green xcodebuild is not enough: with a stale build or a wrong test name it
# runs NOTHING and exits 0 (M3 review). Every test in the file must pass.
PASSED=$(grep -cE "Test Case .*TailnetHarnessTests.* passed" "$LOG_DIR/test.log" || true)
if [[ $TEST_RC -eq 0 && "$PASSED" -ne "$EXPECTED" ]]; then
    echo "error: $PASSED of $EXPECTED TailnetHarnessTests passed (a stale build? try --build)" >&2
    TEST_RC=1
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------- login-link scan --
# The login tests make tsnet log its login link ("AuthURL is ...", "go to:
# ..."), and the node log keeps tsnet's lines on disk (M8.3). A link is a
# login for whoever holds it: nothing on disk may hold one (R29 review).
#
# The scan looks for the LITERAL links the harness minted this run -- GET
# /state lists them as loginLinks -- never for a shape of its own. The first
# version matched /auth/[0-9a-f]{16,}, the one shape upstream's testcontrol
# ever issued, and the harness now mints hostile shapes by default
# (testing/tsnet-harness/authpath.go: mixed case, hyphens, 3-5 groups)
# precisely because a rule written for one shape passes by construction on
# the next; against those links the old regex found nothing and said "ok"
# (review, 2026-09-23). A literal cannot drift.
#
# Validated twice: the harness must list at least one link, or there is no
# secret to look for and the scan proves nothing; and tsnet.log must hold the
# REDACTED form (/auth/…), or the links never reached the log and the scan
# proves nothing either. That needs the LAST test to log in
# (testRequireAuthLogin… does): a reset deletes the node logs, so
# testAResetExpiresTheNodeAtControl sorts early.
say "no login link in the app container"
CONTAINER=$(xcrun simctl get_app_container "$UDID" net.lixom.latchkey data 2>/dev/null || true)
LINKS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/login-link-secrets.txt"
if ! minted_login_secrets > "$LINKS_FILE"; then
    echo "error: could not read the minted login links from the harness ($HARNESS_API/state)" >&2
    TEST_RC=1
fi
LINK_COUNT=$(grep -c . "$LINKS_FILE" || true)
if [[ -z "$CONTAINER" ]]; then
    echo "error: app container not found" >&2; TEST_RC=1
elif [[ "$LINK_COUNT" -lt 1 ]]; then
    echo "error: the harness lists no login link for this run (loginLinks is empty), so there is" >&2
    echo "       no secret to scan for and 'no login link on disk' cannot be established." >&2
    echo "       Did a login test run against this harness generation?" >&2
    TEST_RC=1
else
    # One fixed-string pattern per secret -- the segment after /auth/, so a
    # link written in any other form (path only, another host) is a hit too;
    # case-insensitively, so a store that folds case cannot hide one.
    PATTERNS=()
    while IFS= read -r secret; do PATTERNS+=(-e "$secret"); done < "$LINKS_FILE"
    # grep exits 0 on a match, 1 on none and 2 on an error -- and `if grep
    # ...; then leak; else ok` read 1 and 2 alike as ok, so an unreadable
    # file or a missing directory printed "ok" over a real hit (review,
    # 2026-09-23: grep returns 2 even when it also matched). The matches and
    # the status are judged separately.
    SCAN_RC=0
    grep -rlaFi "${PATTERNS[@]}" "$CONTAINER/Library" "$CONTAINER/tmp" \
        > "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt" 2> "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt.err" || SCAN_RC=$?
    if [[ -s "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt" ]]; then
        echo "error: a login link was written to disk:" >&2
        sed "s|$CONTAINER/|    |" "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt" >&2
        TEST_RC=1
    fi
    if [[ $SCAN_RC -ge 2 ]]; then
        echo "error: the scan could not read everything it was asked to (grep exit $SCAN_RC):" >&2
        sed 's/^/    /' "$LOG_DIR/login-link-leaks.txt.err" | head -5 >&2
        echo "error: the disk scan is incomplete, so 'no login link on disk' is not established" >&2
        TEST_RC=1
    elif [[ $SCAN_RC -eq 1 ]]; then
        if ! grep -rqa "/auth/…" "$CONTAINER/Library/Application Support/"*/Logs/tsnet.log* 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "error: no redacted login link in tsnet.log, so the scan proved nothing" >&2
            TEST_RC=1
        else
            echo "    ok (all of Library + tmp, searched for $LINK_COUNT minted link(s) literally; tsnet.log holds them redacted)"
        fi
    fi
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ summary --
ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))
if [[ $TEST_RC -ne 0 ]]; then
    xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot "$LOG_DIR/failure.png" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    cp "$TSNET/.run/"*.log "$HARNESS/.run/"*.log "$LOG_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || true
    curl -s "$HARNESS_API/state" > "$LOG_DIR/harness-state.json" 2>/dev/null || true
    say "FAILED in ${ELAPSED}s — logs, screenshot and xcresult in $LOG_DIR"
    exit 1
fi
say "passed in ${ELAPSED}s (budget: 300s)"
if [[ $ELAPSED -gt 300 ]]; then
    say "WARNING: over the L2 budget of 5 minutes"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint the test CA and leaf certificate the offline harness serves TLS with.
#
# Idempotent: regenerates only when something is missing or --force is passed.
# Everything it writes is gitignored.
#
# Two things iOS is strict about, both already encoded in ca.cnf / leaf.cnf and
# repeated here because they are the failures people hit:
#
#   * The CA MUST carry `keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign`. Without it,
#     iOS rejects the whole chain with "CA cert does not include key usage
#     extension" — which reads like a trust-store problem and is not.
#   * The leaf MUST carry `subjectAltName`. iOS ignores CN entirely, so a
#     certificate that openssl and curl are perfectly happy with still fails on
#     device with a generic handshake error.
#
# Outputs (all in this directory):
#   ca.key, ca.pem      the test root
#   ca.der              the same root in DER, for `simctl keychain add-root-cert`
#   server.key          the leaf's private key
#   server.pem          leaf + CA, in that order, for dashboard.py
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

FORCE=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--force" ]] && FORCE=1

if [[ $FORCE -eq 0 && -f ca.pem && -f ca.der && -f server.pem && -f server.key ]]; then
    # Regenerate anyway if the leaf has expired or expires within a day —
    # a silently expired fixture produces a TLS error that looks like a
    # proxy bug and costs an hour.
    # ...and if leaf.cnf changed since the leaf was minted (a new SAN would
    # otherwise never reach the certificate).
    if [[ leaf.cnf -nt server.pem ]]; then
        echo "leaf.cnf is newer than the leaf; regenerating"
    elif openssl x509 -checkend 86400 -noout -in server.pem >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "certs present and valid; use --force to regenerate"
        exit 0
    else
        echo "leaf certificate has expired or is about to; regenerating"
    fi
fi

echo "==> test root CA"
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \
    -keyout ca.key -out ca.pem \
    -days 3650 -config ca.cnf >/dev/null 2>&1
openssl x509 -in ca.pem -outform der -out ca.der

echo "==> leaf for dash.tail-scale.ts.net / gw.tail-scale.ts.net / dash.localtest.me / localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1"
echo "    and F6's mapped hosts: esm.sh / esm.sh.away.example / esm.shady.example / fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com"
openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \
    -keyout server.key -out server.csr \
    -subj "/CN=dash.tail-scale.ts.net" >/dev/null 2>&1
openssl x509 -req -in server.csr \
    -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial \
    -out leaf.pem -days 825 \
    -extfile leaf.cnf -extensions ext >/dev/null 2>&1

# dashboard.py hands this straight to `SSLContext.load_cert_chain`, which wants
# the leaf first and the issuer after it.
cat leaf.pem ca.pem > server.pem
rm -f server.csr leaf.pem

echo "==> verifying"
openssl verify -CAfile ca.pem server.pem >/dev/null
# Fail loudly here rather than inside a simulator, where the same mistake
# surfaces as an opaque -1200 and no explanation.
openssl x509 -in ca.pem -noout -text | grep -q "Certificate Sign" \
    || { echo "error: CA is missing keyCertSign — iOS will reject it" >&2; exit 1; }
openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -text | grep -q "DNS:dash.tail-scale.ts.net" \
    || { echo "error: leaf is missing subjectAltName — iOS ignores CN" >&2; exit 1; }
openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -text | grep -q "DNS:dash.localtest.me" \
    || { echo "error: leaf is missing dash.localtest.me — the anti-leak test (R10) needs it" >&2; exit 1; }
for name in esm.sh esm.sh.away.example esm.shady.example fonts.googleapis.com fonts.gstatic.com; do
    openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -text | grep -qE "DNS:${name//./\\.}(,|\$)" \
        || { echo "error: leaf is missing $name — F6's leak tests need it served, not refused" >&2; exit 1; }
done
# The M2 mismatch test needs a tailnet name this leaf does NOT cover. A
# wildcard would cover it, and did once (M3). Read the SAN text rather than
# use -checkhost, which macOS's LibreSSL does not have: there it printed
# nothing and the guard passed without checking (M3 review).
SANS=$(openssl x509 -in server.pem -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name" | tail -1)
[[ -n "$SANS" ]] || { echo "error: could not read the leaf's subjectAltName" >&2; exit 1; }
if grep -qE 'DNS:\*|DNS:wrong\.tail-scale\.ts\.net' <<<"$SANS"; then
    echo "error: leaf covers wrong.tail-scale.ts.net (a wildcard or the name itself) — the certificate-mismatch test needs it not to" >&2; exit 1
fi

echo "ok: ca.pem, ca.der, server.pem, server.key"
echo
echo "Trust the CA in a booted simulator with:"
echo "    xcrun simctl keychain booted add-root-cert $(pwd)/ca.der"

[req]
distinguished_name=dn
[dn]
[ext]
# dash.tail-scale.ts.net  the fixture tailnet's gateway, reached through the stub
#                         proxy (NXDOMAIN in public DNS, so it can only work
#                         proxied)
# dash.localtest.me       a PUBLIC name that resolves to 127.0.0.1 and ::1. The
#                         anti-leak test's origin (R10): unlike a .ts.net name, a
#                         leaked direct connection to it would SUCCEED, so the
#                         test can actually detect one
#                         Also the L2 tsnet harness's dash peer (R17), which
#                         forwards to the same dashboard.
# gw.tail-scale.ts.net    the fake KiroCrew gateway serving the real bundle
#                         (fake_gateway.py, M4 / R19)
# NOT *.tail-scale.ts.net, though R17 suggested it: the wildcard also covers
#                         wrong.tail-scale.ts.net, the M2 certificate-name-
#                         mismatch fixture, and that test then fails for the
#                         right reason. Add each new gateway name explicitly.
# localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1  the control plane of the tests themselves
# esm.sh, esm.sh.away.example, esm.shady.example, fonts.googleapis.com,
#                         fonts.gstatic.com  F6 §6: the stub proxy maps each to
#                         the fake dashboard, so each would be SERVED -- and
#                         counted by Host -- if the app's rule list allowed it.
#                         A load that fails on the certificate instead would make
#                         a zero count prove nothing. This leaf is trusted only in
#                         the test simulator.
subjectAltName=DNS:dash.tail-scale.ts.net,DNS:gw.tail-scale.ts.net,DNS:dash.localtest.me,DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1,IP:::1,DNS:esm.sh,DNS:esm.sh.away.example,DNS:esm.shady.example,DNS:fonts.googleapis.com,DNS:fonts.gstatic.com
extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth
basicConstraints=CA:FALSE
DiscoveryTests.swift
LatchkeyUITests.swift
LifecycleHarnessTests.swift
OfflineHarnessTests.swift
SessionTests.swift
ShareTests.swift
TailnetHarnessTests.swift
